schemes.description: A continuing license scheme where BIS grants permission to use the ISI mark after successful testing and factory inspection, followed by periodic surveillance for the life of the license.
process_steps: Submit application to BIS with product samples and factory details
Product testing at a BIS-recognized laboratory
Factory inspection to verify production consistency
License grant and ISI mark usage permission
schemes.typical_timeline: 2-4 months for first-time applicants, depending on product category and lab availability

schemes.description: A one-time registration scheme (renewed periodically) based on lab test reports, used mainly for electronics and IT goods. Does not require an ISI mark; instead uses a registration number (R-Number) displayed on the product.
process_steps: Get product tested at a BIS-recognized or approved laboratory
Submit test report and product details via the BIS CRS online portal
Display registration number and CRS marking on product and packaging
schemes.typical_timeline: 4-8 weeks, largely dependent on lab testing turnaround

schemes.description: A purity certification scheme for precious metal jewellery, requiring jewellers to register with BIS and get items hallmarked at a BIS-recognized Assaying & Hallmarking Centre (AHC).
process_steps: Jeweller registers with BIS (one-time registration, now largely mandatory for jewellers selling hallmarked jewellery)
Jewellery items are sent to a BIS-recognized Assaying & Hallmarking Centre
Items are tested for purity and marked with the HUID (Hallmark Unique Identification) number
Hallmarked item carries the BIS mark, purity grade, AHC mark, and unique HUID number
schemes.typical_timeline: Registration: 15-30 days. Hallmarking of individual batches: typically 1-2 days at the AHC
